packed_overlap.prep_ignored: packed_overlap launches every job without its preparation (prep.scripted_s is not paid), so for a task with preparation it is a lower bound on a schedule, not a schedule; bar 2 compares the brief-only policy with the best feasible preparation order instead

feasible_best.how: the best of all orders of the recipes under runner/scripted/agent.py's one-preparer rule (one blocking preparer; after each preparation every prepared job that fits on the four GPUs is launched; a recipe's jobs share one command), on that run's own measured preparation spans and job durations; survey/h4-feasible-best-2026-10-24/W0-h4-measure-r2.json and the feasible_best.py beside it. The run's own order simulates to 9,440.2 s against its 9,438.9 s
feasible_best.use: bars 2 and 4-6 read makespan to the last job's end / feasible_best_s; bar 2 = 1.059. The scorer's hindsight bound releases every job at 0 s, since a job's launch names only its training script, so it holds no preparation
